[Testing] `version343Test` and `version344Test` are single-test constructor compatibility variants that emit the same Protostellar telemetry. They remain collection-enabled here, so `check -PcollectMetadata=true` can merge duplicate compatibility output into the default profile; exclude both along with the unit suite.

[Testing] `version23Test` is a one-test API compatibility regression, and `version23TestPreviewSemconv` is its generated semconv copy. Both still inherit collection here, so `check -PcollectMetadata=true` can merge nonrepresentative telemetry into the default/preview profiles; exclude both tasks.

[Testing] `testReceiveSpansDisabled` is a filtered suppression-only regression task, but this condition leaves collection enabled for it. Running this module's `check` with `-PcollectMetadata=true` therefore merges nonrepresentative telemetry into the default profile; exclude that task as well.

[Testing] `testReceiveSpansDisabled` runs only `Jms3SuppressReceiveSpansTest`, so it is a regression-only suppression task. This condition still enables collection for it during `check -PcollectMetadata=true`, causing its output to be merged into default metadata; exclude it too.

[Testing] The filtered `testReceiveSpansDisabled` task exercises only the receive-span suppression regression, yet this condition still allows it to collect under `check -PcollectMetadata=true`. Exclude it so that its telemetry is not merged into the default Spring JMS profile.

Applies the telemetry collection rules proposed in #20454 that exclude unit tests and regression-only variants from metadata collection, including when they inherit collection settings.

Disables collection for the affected unit suites and filtered default-enablement tests, even with `-PcollectMetadata=true`. They remain in `check`, and representative integration suites continue to collect telemetry.

Refs #20546.
metadata.title: Exclude nonrepresentative test tasks from metadata collection
